newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end down in roller-coaster trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end down in roller-coaster trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Tuesday in very volatile trading amid a power struggle between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.44 percent, or 1.31 points, to 293.30 on all-share turnover of 220 million shekels against 264 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.51 percent lower at 302.36.
"All traders were listening to the radio today trying to figure out what was going on," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.
The market was reacting to news that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would announce later on Tuesday a widening of the currency band as part of a package of economic measures.

"Investors are very confused and it is hard to predict which decision is good for the market. There is much uncertainty and all the rumours had a psychological impact on trading," said Eli Nahum head of trading at Zannex Securities.

Early Tuesday morning Netanyahu announced that he had agreed at an all-night meeting with Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel to a package of budget cuts and foreign currency liberalisations. The forex reforms will raise the ceilings on overseas investment for institutional investors and companies.
Benjamin Netanyahu called a special cabinet meeting for later on Tuesday to present a compromise in a dispute over widening the exchange rate band.

The central bank supports a widening in order to alleviate pressure to support the basket rate, which has been trading at or close to its seven percent limit all this year. But Meridor opposes a widening while interest rates are high.
"Trading was very volatile today. The session opened with a decline of 0.6 percent. Later the market rose by 0.3 percent before it fell and rose twice more," Halpern said.
Nahum added that the market is very nervous. "The market is at a record high and it is only normal that it is so volatile on such a day," he said.

Halpern said that the market hoped that the central bank and the Treasury would reach a compromise that will include a moderate widening of the currency band in return for a rate cut. "It seems now that Meridor is going to win the battle and they will not widen the band to 15 percent (from seven). I am sure Meridor will remain in office," he said.
Israel's media has speculated that Netanyahu intended to reshuffle his ministers, moving Ariel Sharon from infrastructure to the finance post.
Traders said that once an agreement is reached the market is expected to continue rising.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which climbed 1.5 percent to 562 agorot on turnover of 24.5 million shekels; Koor Industries, which fell 1.0 percent to 32,187 agorot on volume of 17.5 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.0 percent to 20,630 agorot on volume of 6 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
